describe: One shared, bounded, versioned corpus of engineering-slice-plan.v1/v2 whole plans used to prove that the server validator (mcp-server/src/engineering-runtime.js requirePlan) and the portable validator (tools/room-bridge/engineering_passport.py validate_engineering_slice_plan) accept and refuse exactly the same inputs. Every vector is a declarative patch over one named base plan, so neither language reconstructs a fixture and neither restates a validation rule.
seam_notes: Plan registration is the one seam both validators expose publicly with the same input shape, so equivalence is claimed there and nowhere else.

The contract-versus-issued-binding refusal is NOT a shared public seam. On the server it lives inside admitEngineeringSlice, which needs a database connection; in the portable validator it lives inside build_engineering_slice_packet, which needs a full execution-envelope fixture of a different shape. Nothing public on either side takes the same two arguments, so this corpus records the three contradictions (read_only true under a write profile, a production environment, an attended_human route) as ACCEPTED BY BOTH plan validators, which is the true shared behavior, instead of inventing a parity claim the exports cannot support.
Ops are pure data manipulation (set/delete/append/reorder). They never encode a validation rule.

Identifiers are matched against the closed regex exactly as written. The portable validator (engineering_passport._str with identifier=True) and the SQL validators have always matched the raw value; the server validator matched a trimmed copy while the plan kept, sealed and compared the raw string, so a padded identifier registered on the server alone. engineering-slice-plan.v2 now matches the raw value on the server too, using the SAME regex and the same contract version: this is a bug correction inside the existing identifier rule, not a policy change or a new version. Legacy engineering-slice-plan.v1 keeps its exact previous trimming acceptance, because requirePlan re-runs against the stored append-only plan row on every read path; that legacy behavior is recorded in divergence_vectors rather than omitted. A padded identifier is always refused, never normalised into an accepted identity, on either version.

The identifier rule reaches identifiers only. Prose fields (objective, definition_of_done, scope_boundary, rationale, measurement note, objective_summary, failure detection and compensation, completion predicate) keep their exact accepted whitespace behavior in both validators; identity.v2.padded-objective-is-still-prose pins that.

seal_modes.reseal: recompute plan_digest over the patched plan (the normal producer path)
seal_modes.as_is: leave the digest that was computed over the UNPATCHED base, which is genuinely stale once ops change content, and which stays deleted if an op deleted it
seal_modes.literal: use the vector's own plan_digest value verbatim

divergence_vectors.describe: DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly and deliberately excluded from the equivalence claim. The portable validator has always refused duplicate ordinals for every plan version. The server validator historically accepted them, and requirePlan re-runs against the STORED append-only plan row on every read path, so refusing them for v1 now would strand an already registered passport rather than repair it. The server therefore binds the refusal to engineering-slice-plan.v2 only. See the header comment in mcp-server/src/engineering-runtime.js.
DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. A v1 slice depending on itself stays readable in the server validator and is refused by the portable one, for the same append-only reason.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. A legacy v1 two-slice cycle stays readable in the server validator (and every slice on the cycle stays blocked forever, which is the previous behavior unchanged) and is refused by the portable one.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly and deliberately excluded from the equivalence claim. The portable validator (engineering_passport._str with identifier=True) and the SQL validators have always matched the closed identifier regex against the RAW value; the server validator matched it against a trimmed copy while the plan kept, sealed and compared the raw string, so a padded legacy v1 slice_ref registered here. requirePlan re-runs against the STORED append-only plan row on every read path, so refusing it for v1 now would strand an already registered passport instead of repairing it. The server therefore binds exact identifiers to engineering-slice-plan.v2 only. THE GATE IS THE DECLARED PLAN VERSION, NOT THE ROW'S AGE: a plan NEWLY registered as engineering-slice-plan.v1 keeps this permissive legacy acceptance too, not only a stored one, because requirePlan is one predicate over one input and cannot tell a fresh registration from a stored row -- refusing new v1 registrations alone would make the same plan registerable and then unreadable, or the reverse. Narrowing what a v1 producer may newly register is a separate policy change with its own producers to migrate and is deliberately out of scope for this corpus, which records the behavior as it is. The vector's expect_javascript therefore states plain acceptance at registration. The v2 counterpart of this shape is identity.v2.slice-ref-leading-and-trailing-space, which BOTH validators refuse. The padded identifier is never trimmed into an accepted identity on either version.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. The same legacy trimming acceptance applies to the plan's work_request.id binding. The v2 counterpart is identity.v2.work-request-id-padded, which both validators refuse.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. The same legacy trimming acceptance applies to accepted_plan_revision.id. The v2 counterpart is identity.v2.accepted-plan-revision-id-padded, which both validators refuse.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. One vector stands for the whole legacy identifier-array loop: declared_resource_refs, declared_component_refs and declared_plan_step_refs are validated by the same call in both validators, so all three behave identically here. dependency_refs is deliberately NOT in this family, because a padded dependency reference matches no slice and is refused by both (identity.v1.dependency-ref-padded). The v2 counterpart is identity.v2.declared-resource-ref-padded, which both validators refuse.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. forbidden_change_refs carries identifiers through the same legacy loop. The v2 counterpart is identity.v2.forbidden-change-ref-padded, which both validators refuse.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. A legacy v1 planned check reference is an identifier the server trimmed before matching, and v1 has no design contract whose planned_check_refs binding would have caught the mismatch downstream. The v2 counterpart is identity.v2.planned-check-ref-padded, which both validators refuse.

DOCUMENTED LEGACY DIVERGENCE, asserted exactly. Nested typed evidence carries an identifier too, and the legacy server path trimmed it. The v2 counterpart is identity.v2.baseline-evidence-ref-padded, which both validators refuse.
